sentences.text: The animal is known from a single partial skull found in the Melovatskaya Formation of the Volgograd Region in Russia.
Researchers identified it as an ornithurine due to the lack of a postorbital bone, thin skull roof, and high fusion between skull bones.
The genus Cerebavis was described by Kurochkin and colleagues in 2006.
The fossil was initially misidentified as a fossilized brain of an enantiornithean bird, but in 2011 researchers reinterpreted it as an incomplete and abraded skull rather than a brain cast.
The brain structure resembles that of living birds, lacking a large pineal gland and having olfactory bulbs of expected size.
The brain shows unusual characteristics, including a well-developed olfactory system and a large cerebrum.
Despite its advanced shape, the animal seemingly lacked a wulst, suggesting its brain was not fully modern.
However, the brain could show a relatively large parietal eye and pineal gland.
Cerebavis is classified within the order Saurischia and the suborder Theropoda.
It is placed in the unranked family Avialae and the unranked clade Ornithurae, which serves as its parent group.
Cerebavis lived during the middle Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous period, between 99.6 and 93.5 million years ago.

A 2021 redescription of Borogovia suggested Cerebavis might be a scansoriopterygid located at the base of the non-avian Oviraptorosauria clade. In 2011, the specimen was regarded as potentially a nomen dubium. It is debated whether the animal is an ornithurine or a scansoriopterygid at the base of non-avian Oviraptorosauria.
